design.text: Two-part trial: Part 1 was a 14-day open-label responsiveness phase; Part 2 was a 6-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase with 1:1 randomization and ascending doses given every 2 weeks (20 mg/kg QD for Weeks 1-2, 40 mg/kg QD for Weeks 3-4, and 60 mg/kg QD for Weeks 5-6).

citations.quote: Part 1 was a 14-day, open-label trial to determine sepiapterin responsiveness.
Part 2 was a 6-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of sepiapterin in adult and pediatric patients with PKU.
were enrolled in Part 2, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled portion with 1:1 randomization between sepiapterin and placebo.
Participants in the sepiapterin treatment arm received 20 mg/kg QD for Weeks 1 and 2, 40 mg/kg QD for Weeks 3 and 4, and then 60 mg/kg QD for Weeks 5 and 6, sequentially.

population.text: Pediatric and adult participants aged 1 to 61 years with PKU who were determined to be sepiapterin-responsive.

citations.quote: PKU-003: A two-part trial in 157 participants aged 1 to 61 years with PKU.
Only those participants with \ge 15\% reduction from baseline in blood Phe level, with sepiapterin responsiveness defined as \ge 30\% reduction from baseline, were enrolled in Part 2.

endpoint.text: Mean change in blood Phe levels from baseline to Weeks 5 and 6 in the Part 2 double-blind phase.

citations.quote: Mean change in blood Phe levels from baseline to Weeks 5 and 6 in the Part 2 DB phase

n.text: 110 patients randomized and treated in Part 2 (Sepiapterin N=56, Placebo N=54).

citations.quote: 110 patients randomized and treated in Part 2
Part 2: Sepiapterin (N=56), Placebo (N=54)

result.text: Statistically significant reduction in mean blood Phe: least squares mean difference -395.87 umol/L (95% CI -463.07, -328.66); blood Phe decreased by 410 umol/L in the sepiapterin group vs 16 umol/L in placebo.

citations.quote: The least squares mean difference between sepiapterin and placebo groups was -395.87 \mu\text{mol/L} with 95% CI: (-463.07, -328.66).
The observed mean blood Phe level decreased by 410 \mu\text{mol/L} (from 646 \mu\text{mol/L} to 236 \mu\text{mol/L}) in the sepiapterin group compared to 16 \mu\text{mol/L}

indication.text: Treatment of hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) in adult and pediatric patients 1 month of age and older with sepiapterin-responsive phenylketonuria (PKU), used in conjunction with a Phe-restricted diet.

citations.quote: SEPHIENCE is indicated for the treatment of hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) in adult and pediatric patients 1 month of age and older with sepiapterin-responsive phenylketonuria (PKU). SEPHIENCE is to be used in conjunction with a phenylalanine (Phe)-restricted diet.

target_moa.text: Sepiapterin is a synthetic precursor of BH4, converted via the pterin salvage pathway (sepiapterin reductase and dihydrofolate reductase); BH4 is an essential cofactor that activates phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), the enzyme deficient in PKU.

citations.quote: Sepiapterin is a precursor of BH4, which is a co-factor for phenylalanine hydroxylase enzyme that is deficient in patients with PKU.
Sepiapterin is converted to BH4 via the pterin salvage pathway, mediated by sepiapterin reductase (SR) and dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR).

modality.text: Small molecule (synthetic form of endogenous sepiapterin, an oral powder).

citations.quote: Sepiapterin is a synthetic form of endogenous sepiapterin that serves as a substrate for BH4 synthesis.

## SEPHIENCE (sepiapterin) oral powder
## Initial U.S. Approval: 2025

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=2% and greater than placebo) were diarrhea, headache, abdominal pain, hypophenylalaninemia, feces discoloration, and oropharyngeal pain. Warnings and precautions include increased bleeding and hypophenylalaninemia.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions with SEPHIENCE (\ge 2\% and greater than placebo) were diarrhea, headache, abdominal pain, hypophenylalaninemia, feces discoloration, and oropharyngeal pain. (6.1)
- **Increased Bleeding:** SEPHIENCE may increase the risk of bleeding. Consider treatment interruption in patients with active bleeding. (5.1)
In Trial 1 Part 2, hypophenylalaninemia was seen in 5.4% (2/37) of sepiapterin-treated pediatric patients and in no adult patients.

vote.text: No advisory committee was convened; no scientific, technical, or policy issues arose that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.

citations.quote: The marketing application for sepiapterin was not taken to an FDA advisory committee because no scientific, technical, or policy issues arose that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.

detail.text: The multidisciplinary team concluded the benefit-risk balance is favorable and recommended approval; no prior complete response letter for this application is described.

citations.quote: In summary, the multidisciplinary team concludes that the benefit-risk balance of sepiapterin is favorable and recommends approval. The Divisional and signatory authorities concur with this recommendation.

basis.text: A Preliminary Breakthrough Therapy Designation Request advice teleconference was held, but the Agency indicated a successful designation would require more information; no breakthrough therapy designation was granted.

citations.quote: the Agency informed PTC that a successful breakthrough therapy designation
request would require more information to show that sepiapterin could provide a substantial improvement over existing therapy (e.g., Kuvan) for the treatment of PKU.

basis.text: A Fast Track designation request was submitted with the IND but was denied on September 22, 2021.

citations.quote: Included with the IND submission was a request for a Fast Track designation, which was denied on September 22, 2021, because the submitted data were not adequate to support the potential to address an unmet medical need in the context of available therapies for PKU.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation granted March 4, 2021 for sepiapterin for the treatment of HPA.

summary.text: SEPHIENCE was approved via a standard review NDA with Orphan Drug Designation (and rare pediatric disease designation); Fast Track was denied and breakthrough therapy was not granted, and the approval was not an accelerated approval.
